deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected pencil draft of a letter by Riemann, beginning 'Hochverehrter Herr Hofrath'. It recommends Richard Dedekind for the professorship at the Collegium Carolinum in Braunschweig. Dedekind moved there from the Zürich Polytechnikum in 1862, so the draft dates to about 1862.

The addressee is probably Wilhelm Weber, a Hofrath. This is my inference: Riemann signs as 'ergebenster Schüler und College', which fits Weber, but it is not certain.

Content, paraphrased:
(1) Riemann thanks the addressee for the news that there is some prospect of winning Dedekind back for his native country. He thanks him for his confidence and agrees to give his view of Dedekind's suitability for the Carolinum post.
(2) Through many years of oral and written exchange, Riemann has come to know Dedekind's character, his zeal, and the skill and elegance with which he moves through scientific investigations and presents their results. He wishes Dedekind more leisure for research than he currently has.
(3) Riemann has no doubt about Dedekind as a teacher. During their shared time as Privatdozenten in Göttingen, beside the eminent teachers there, Dedekind had little room for a wide sphere of activity. Even so, some students heard his lectures with profit. Riemann names Prof. (Eduard) Selling in Würzburg as an example.
(4) Later, in Zürich, Dedekind had ample opportunity to work in a larger circle and develop his great gifts.
(5) Riemann therefore concludes that Dedekind combines all the conditions that make his election to the Carolinum a thoroughly happy one and promise the finest results.
(6) The letter closes 'mit vollkommenster Hochachtung ... Ihr ergebenster Schüler und College, B. Riemann'.

A lower-right marginal note ('ich würde ...') is not legible enough to read.

The neighbouring pages are drafts about the actuarial review of the Hannover widows' fund (c. 1857). They are unrelated to this letter, apart from Riemann's habit of drafting letters on spare sheets.

results.what: Letter of recommendation by Riemann for Dedekind's appointment to the Collegium Carolinum, Braunschweig (c. 1862). It mentions Selling as a former auditor of Dedekind's Göttingen lectures.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely biographical: a recommendation letter for Dedekind with no mathematics. Riemann's support for Dedekind is well known. The specific mention of Selling corroborates the known fact that Selling (with Auwers) attended Dedekind's Göttingen lectures, including those on Galois theory. A draft of this letter is a minor archival detail of interest for Dedekind biography, not for the history of mathematics proper.
transcription_corrections: The signature is probably 'B. Riemann'. The initial looks like 'L.' in the image, but that is very likely a cursive B.
'Tauglichkeit' may instead read 'Tüchtigkeit' or 'Befähigung'. The superscript replacement over 'Befähigung' is uncertain.
The 'Selling' passage is reasonably clear: 'In dieser Beziehung dürfte außer Dedekind's Schülern Prof. Selling in Würzburg zu nennen sein.'
'[-Collegen-]' in the Zürich paragraph appears to be a crossed-out word ending in '-gen' (possibly 'Collegen'). The following reading 'verwandte und begabte Schüler' is plausible.
In the closing, 'durchaus glückliche' is preceded by an inserted 'als eine' (or 'als ein ganz'). The struck word before 'vollkommensten Hochachtung' is likely 'Mit'.
